observation.description: There is no push-notification boundary for a mobile Snapback app on 0.1.7, in the mobile-specific sense the EXPO-09 receipt check asks about: no device-token registration surface anywhere in the packaged closure, no APNs/FCM or expo-notifications integration (or even a mention) in the guide, and the generated capability manifest ships notifications:false. The generic gap is already owned (the guide capability index carries backend.notifications as design-only with an explicit notifications gap, LLP 0045), but the mobile carrier adds two compounding blockers this finding pins: (1) even the app-authored bridge - an action posting to a push provider - is unauthorable on packaged 0.1.7 because the outbound effect lane is broken (0137-a4-f1; the plain ctx.fetch fix landed on main at 117dcae2 AFTER the 0.1.7 publication and is not in this arm's pinned packages), and (2) with no hosted mobile path (0137-a1expo-f5) there is nowhere a production push relay could run. An event product's 'tell my guests' moment therefore has no product lane at all on mobile; the A4 backend's notifyIntents/notifyAttempts ledger is application code around a boundary that does not exist.
evidence: guide/capabilities.md (backend.notifications row: design-only, explicit notifications gap)

competitorOutcome.description: Firebase ships Cloud Messaging as a first-class mobile product: device-token registration, APNs/FCM delivery, and server-side send APIs are documented core features of the RN/mobile SDK surface.

mustNotRegress: The honest capability manifest (notifications:false) and the app-side intent/attempt ledger pattern's ambiguity discipline - when a push boundary ships, ambiguous provider outcomes must stay distinct and retryable rather than being silently absorbed.
smallestCoherentFix: Sequenced behind the owners: first the outbound action lane on the packaged closure (a4-f1, already fixed on main), then a documented device-token registration + provider-relay recipe (expo-notifications or raw APNs/FCM) as the guide's mobile notification page, with the first-class notifications capability (LLP 0045) as the eventual product boundary.
acceptanceWitness: An Expo simulator app registers a push token through a documented Snapback path and an RSVP change produces one inspectable delivery attempt at a push provider boundary (simulator receipt may stub APNs; the boundary and ledger are the witnessed facts).
